name: Ross Klopf

summary.text: Ross Klopf is a civil engineer from Lakewood, Colorado, with decades of experience in transportation and water-resources engineering. He has been a Libertarian Party member since 2016.

experience.text: Civil engineer with decades of experience in transportation and water resources engineering.
Unsuccessful Libertarian candidate for Colorado's 7th Congressional District in 2022 and for state House District 28 in 2018.

education_focus.text: Klopf's top issue is reading comprehension; he points to countries such as Portugal that have improved reading outcomes and suggests giving students reading material they enjoy even if it is not considered a classic.
On charter schools, he says 'lower birth rates and declining student enrollment are not valid reasons to deny a charter school application.'
On Proposition NN and Amendment 87, he says any new funding measure should specify what share goes to classrooms and teacher pay and include an independent audit committee and a sunset clause.

positions.source_title: 9 questions for Colorado's State Board of Education candidates this year
positions.quote: I do not support Amendment 87 for the same reasons described above for Proposition NN. In addition, I believe it could negatively affect Colorado businesses.
positions.note: He proposes conditions (an audit committee, a sunset clause) under which a similar measure could win his support, so coded as qualified rather than unqualified disagreement.

positions.source_title: 9 questions for Colorado's State Board of Education candidates this year
positions.quote: This measure was placed on the ballot by the state legislature, and I believe it is better than Amendment 87. Although funding is a significant issue for many schools, I do not support this measure.
